### S02: arXiv:2610.29941 v2, Abstract, sentences 4-6
PDF p. 1; TeX line 73 of `src/2610.29941v2/research.tex`; Q3.

> Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals.

### S03: arXiv:2610.29941 v2, Abstract, last sentence

### S33: arXiv:2610.29941 v2, Sec. VI, paragraph 5
PDF p. 9; TeX line 424 of `src/2610.29941v2/research.tex`; Q3.

> Above about $29\%$ of the extremal angular momentum ($v_e\approx0.46$) the throat's equator lies inside an ergoregion. Horizonless rotating objects with an ergoregion are generically subject to a slow nonaxisymmetric instability~\cite{friedman1978,cardoso2008}; our runs, started from axisymmetric data, bound only axisymmetric growth. Only the drainhole family ($C=1$) was evolved; the symmetric family enters through the solver validation alone.
